name: Crusoe
summary: Crusoe builds vertically integrated AI infrastructure, from power and data centres to cloud services.
overview: Crusoe develops AI factories and cloud infrastructure designed around power availability and large-scale compute.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Initial closing announced September 2026 at a $30.9B post-money valuation.

bull_case: Vertical integration across power, campuses, and cloud can make Crusoe a scarce supplier of AI-ready capacity.
bear_case: The model is capital intensive and exposed to construction, power, customer-concentration, and financing-cycle risk.
directory_notes: Power delivery, site execution, and conversion of contracted demand.

intelligence.description: Crusoe builds AI infrastructure from energy generation and data-centre campuses through Crusoe Cloud. Its advantage, if it holds, is solving the power-and-delivery problem that can prevent AI demand from turning into operating capacity.
company: Crusoe started with energy-focused computing and has expanded into a vertically integrated AI-infrastructure platform. It develops and operates large campuses, buys and deploys equipment, and provides cloud capacity to AI-native, hyperscaler, frontier-model, and enterprise customers.
The company raised a $600M Series D at $2.8B in late 2024, then a $1.375B Series E above $10B in 2025. Its September 2026 Series F materially increased the scale of both its financing and valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Crusoe shows how the AI boom is transferring value from software into power, land, construction, networking, and finance. It is a key private comparable for the economics of the emerging AI-factory model.

changed.text: Closed a $600M Series D at a $2.8B valuation to expand AI infrastructure.
Raised $1.375B at a valuation above $10B as AI-compute demand accelerated.
Announced a $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B post-money valuation and $140B+ of total contracted value.

takeaways: Crusoe's differentiation is physical delivery: power, campus construction, and cloud capacity in one platform.
The valuation reflects contracted demand, but converting contracts into operating capacity is capital- and execution-intensive.
Power availability is becoming a more important AI bottleneck than raw chip demand alone.
Financing costs, site permitting, and customer concentration are the central risks.
